statement: In a class of 30, 18 play football and 14 play chess. 6 play both. How many play neither?

choices.misconception: I added 18 and 14 without removing the overlap, then subtracted from 30.
I subtracted the 6 who play both twice instead of once.
I subtracted only the footballers from the class and forgot the chess players entirely.
I found how many play at least one sport and gave that instead of how many play neither.

hints: Fill in the middle of the two circles first.
Draw two overlapping circles and write the 6 who do both in the overlap. The rest of each circle is what is left after taking the overlap out, and everything outside is the answer.
Playing at least one is 18 + 14 - 6 = 26. So 30 - 26 = 4 play neither.

solutions.reliable: Adding 18 and 14 counts the 6 who do both twice, so the number playing at least one is 18 + 14 - 6 = 26. Everyone else plays neither: 30 - 26 = 4. Drawing it confirms the parts: 12 football only, 6 both, 8 chess only, 4 neither - and 12 + 6 + 8 + 4 = 30. The transferable idea: fill the overlap in first, then the rest follows.

whyOnTest: Two overlapping groups is one of the most reliably examined shapes at this level, and the double-counted overlap is the whole difficulty.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
